language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, I'm Chip.
Hi friends! I am Mattie.
I want to show you some special polygons: closed 2-dimensional shapes.
The first one is a rectangular mat. It has four straight sides whose opposites are parallel and have the same length.

backgroundLayers.text:
Lines AB and CD are equal and parallel
Lines AD and BC are equal and parallel
Each angle is 90°

dialog.text: The second shape is a trapezoid. A trapezoid has two parallel sides, but with different lengths.

backgroundLayers.text: Lines AD and bc are parallel

dialog.text: The third shape resembles a kite. It has two different pairs of equal sides that join together.

backgroundLayers.text: Lines BC and CD are equal
Lines AB and AD are equal

dialog.text: The fourth shape is a square, which has 4 equal sides and all 90° angles.

backgroundLayers.text: All sides and all angles are equal

dialog.text: Polygons with equal sides and equal angles are called regular, like these others shown here. All others are irregular.
The last shape is called a parallelogram. Like a rhombus, the opposite sides are parallel - but the sides may not be all equal.

backgroundLayers.text:
Lines AB and DC are equal and parallel
Lines AD and BC are equal and parallel

dialog.text: Each of these special polygons has four sides, so they are quadrilaterals. Quad means 4, and lateral means side.
...and there we go! Now, see if you can work with each of these special quadrilaterals and other polygons.
Hi, I'm Chip.
Hi friends! I am Mattie.
I want to show you some special polygons: closed 2-dimensional shapes.
The first one is a rectangular mat. It has four straight sides whose opposites are parallel and have the same length.
The second shape is a trapezoid. A trapezoid has two parallel sides, but with different lengths.
The third shape resembles a kite. It has two different pairs of equal sides that join together.
The fourth shape is a square, which has 4 equal sides and all 90° angles.
Polygons with equal sides and equal angles are called regular, like these others shown here. All others are irregular.
The last shape is called a parallelogram. Like a rhombus, the opposite sides are parallel - but the sides may not be all equal.
Each of these special polygons has four sides, so they are quadrilaterals. Quad means 4, and lateral means side.
...and there we go! Now, see if you can work with each of these special quadrilaterals and other polygons.
